authorization: Any key for the account; NOT management-only
origin: hand-written from the published OpenAPI schema; every value invented
notes: budgets[] is in enforcement order (guardrail, then workspace, then the key's own limit) and effective_budget is the one that blocks first - here the guardrail budget, whose remaining_usd of 17.5 is the smallest. Summing budgets[] would count one allowance three times. remaining_usd is derived as limit_usd - spend_usd and may be zero or negative, which blocks requests; it is a real state, not a parse error. limit_remaining describes THIS KEY only and is not the account balance. usage_weekly is the current UTC week starting Monday and resets_at is an ISO 8601 UTC instant. is_free_tier means 'has the user paid for credits before', not a plan name. byok_usage* is spend through the user's own upstream keys and does not draw account credits. rate_limit is deprecated. label is already masked by the API; the published example uses the provider's real key prefix, which this corpus deliberately avoids so secret scanners stay clean. This fixture is the organization-owned case: both `organization_id` and `workspace_id` are non-null, and the invented UUID-shaped identifiers are valid hexadecimal so a strict decoder accepts them. SCHEMA RE-VERIFICATION 2026-10-30: the authoritative OpenAPI schema for this route was read at https://openrouter.ai/docs/api/api-reference/api-keys/get-current-api-key. Its `data` object publishes 24 required fields; this fixture carries all of them plus the optional nullable `expires_at`. Three corrections follow. (1) `rate_limit` is not an invented sub-shape: the schema publishes it as an object with three typed, required properties (`interval` string, `requests` integer, `note` string) and marks the object `deprecated: true` with the description "Legacy rate limit information about a key. Will always return -1." That description contradicts the schema's own example values (1h / 1000), which are what this fixture reproduces, so the field must be parsed and discarded and never read as a live rate limit. (2) `organization_id` and `workspace_id` are required and are the documented account and workspace identity: `organization_id` is "null when an individual account owns it" and `workspace_id` is "null when no active workspace resolved for it, for example because the key's workspace was deleted". (3) `is_management_key`, `is_provisioning_key`, `expires_at`, `creator_user_id` and `allowed_data_regions` ARE published schema properties, so their presence is documented rather than unverified; the abbreviated `Key` type in the limits guide simply omits them. `is_provisioning_key` and `rate_limit` are both `deprecated: true`. Two documentation conflicts are recorded rather than resolved: `is_free_tier` is described as "whether the user has paid for credits before" in the limits guide but "Whether this is a free tier API key" in the schema, so it must not be read as a plan name; and the schema documents only 401 and 500 responses for this route, with no 403, unlike GET /api/v1/credits.
